items.title: Metallica Announce 2027 North American Tour Dates
items.summary:
Metallica have added a 12-date North American run in 2027, extending the M72 World Tour that the band launched in 2023 and appeared to close out this past summer. Limp Bizkit and Avatar will open all 12 shows, which are stadium dates rather than the two-night, no-repeat-setlist stands that defined much of the earlier touring.

The run begins May 8th at BC Place in Vancouver and continues through San Diego's Snapdragon Stadium, Sun Bowl Stadium in El Paso, the Alamodome in San Antonio, Razorback Stadium in Fayetteville, Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Carter-Finley Stadium in Raleigh, Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Highmark Stadium in Buffalo, Camp Randall Stadium in Madison, Huntington Bank Field in Cleveland and Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City, where it ends June 19th.

Tickets go through the usual sequence of gates. Metallica's Fan Club pre-sale opens Monday, September 21st at 10 a.m. local time, followed by pre-sales for Citi cardmembers and Verizon customers enrolled in the Verizon Shine loyalty program on September 22nd at 10 a.m. The general on-sale lands Friday, September 25th at 10 a.m. local time via Ticketmaster.

As Consequence reported, the 2027 dates will be the band's first road work after their Las Vegas Sphere residency, Life Burns Faster, which runs from October 2026 through March 2027 across two dozen Thursday and Saturday performances. Every announced Sphere show is scheduled for 8:30 p.m.

Before any of that, Metallica play two shows at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, Connecticut, on November 19th and 21st, marking the venue's 25th anniversary. With the residency bookending the winter and the stadium run picking up in May, the band's calendar is now accounted for well into the summer of 2027.

items.title: Ozzy Osbourne and Black Sabbath’s Final Concert Film Sets October Release Date
items.summary:
The concert film documenting Ozzy Osbourne's final performance with Black Sabbath will reach theaters worldwide on October 28. Titled "Ozzy Black Sabbath: Back to the Beginning," the movie is directed by Ben Wainwright-Pearce, who edited "Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour" for Disney+. Trafalgar Releasing is distributing, and Mercury Studios produced.

The show took place July 5 at Villa Park in Birmingham, Osbourne's home city, drawing 42,000 people in person and roughly 3 million more through a paid livestream. Osbourne played a solo set and then reunited with original Sabbath members Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler and Bill Ward for the first time in two decades. He died on July 22, 2025, 17 days later, following a years-long struggle with Parkinson's disease.

Sharon Osbourne, his wife and manager, described the event's origins in a statement. "Back to the Beginning came about because I asked Ozzy what would really make him happy," she said. "And he said the only thing that would make him happy was if he could perform again and say goodbye to his fans. That's all he wanted to do. He wanted to say goodbye and thank you."

Jason Momoa hosted the concert, which featured performances from Disturbed's David Draiman, Halestorm, Travis Barker, Steven Tyler, Slayer, Pantera, Tool and Alice in Chains. Tim van Someren directed the live event, produced by Jim Parsons, Jamie Silk and Dan Seliger.

Variety reported that tickets go on sale September 24 through backtothebeginning.com. Trafalgar CEO Marc Allenby called the concert "a landmark cultural moment" and said the theatrical release is "an opportunity to further cement Ozzy's legacy and impact."

items.title: Kevin Morby Shares New Single “PBJ”: Stream
items.summary:
Kevin Morby has released a standalone single called "PBJ," arriving with a music video four months after his last album. Aaron Dessner produced the track, which features Andrew Barr on drums and Justin Vernon on electric guitar, with Morby handling vocals, piano, synths and Mellotron.

The title has nothing to do with sandwiches, at least not directly. Morby took it from a phrase a friend used for driving with the windows down and the air conditioning blasting. "I always loved the phrase and have used it ever since," he said in a statement. "I also love a peanut butter and jelly sandwich (and all its variations) and so this is a very fun song for me. An end of summer song. Listen to it with the windows down and the air conditioning up."

The song pairs heat, romance and driving imagery with a more wistful refrain about people coming together before scattering again. Morby is marking the release with a set of food collaborations, including a PBJ ice cream from Van Leeuwen, a cookie at New York's Culture Espresso and a donut from Mr. D's Donut Shop in Kansas.

Consequence reported that "PBJ" follows "Little Wide Open," Morby's eighth studio album, which Dead Oceans released in May. Dessner produced that record as well, and Morby wrote all 13 songs on it.

Morby's touring calendar picks up later this month at Richmond's Iron Blossom festival. He heads to Australia for a run of dates in November, then plays My Morning Jacket's One Big Holiday in Mexico in January and Knoxville's Big Ears Festival in April.

items.title: ‘Resident Evil’ Review: Zach Cregger Brings Style, Humor, And A Game Austin Abrams To Make Smart Original Reboot Of Horror Franchise
items.summary:
Zach Cregger's "Resident Evil" arrives as a full reset of Sony's long-running video game adaptation, and Deadline's review calls it a success on its own terms. Cregger, who wrote the script with Shay Hatten, discarded the franchise's established characters and built a new storyline while keeping a handful of core elements intact. Austin Abrams takes the lead.

Abrams plays Bryan, a medical courier transporting human organs on a snowy Colorado night who accepts a last-minute job for double pay, bound for a hospital in Raccoon City. He hits a woman who runs into the road, tries to get her help, and discovers she is the first of the infected — humans mutating into tentacled creatures. From there the film becomes a sustained chase across a barn, a deserted farmhouse and a trailer, until Umbrella Corporation operatives Maxine (Kali Reis) and Paul (Paul Walter Hauser) pick Bryan up and explain what he is actually carrying.

Deadline's Pete Hammond wrote that he had worried Cregger, coming off "Barbarian" and the Oscar-winning "Weapons," was cashing in on studio IP, and found the opposite. The review singles out Abrams, previously seen in "Wolfs" and as the unhoused character in "Weapons," as the film's engine, calling this his breakout. It also credits Cregger's use of dark comedy as the thing that makes the relentless pacing bearable.

The review praises cinematographer Dariusz Wolski's camerawork alongside the visual effects and makeup teams, and notes the film runs a tight 90 minutes. Hauser's performance is described as hilariously intense.

The cast also includes Zach Cherry and Will Merrick. Producers are Robert Kulzer, Cregger, Roy Lee, Miri Yoon, Victor Hadida, Asad Qizilbash and Carter Swan. The franchise previously spanned roughly eight films, six of them starring Milla Jovovich between 2002 and 2016, plus a 2021 reboot and a Netflix series.

items.title: Which artists dropped out of the Ed Sheeran tour?
items.summary:
Four acts have withdrawn from Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour in the days since Macklemore was removed from the bill over his public support for Palestine. Macklemore said Sheeran, a longtime friend, had been pressured by a group of stadium owners led by Robert Kraft. Sheeran confirmed in his own statement that Kraft and other venue owners approached him, but said the promoter, not he, made the call to drop Macklemore.

Sheeran said he was "appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine" and "not complicit," framing his position as apolitical. That framing did not land as neutral, and the departures followed. The FADER has been tracking which artists have left the tour.

Beoga, the Irish band that served as Sheeran's backing group, announced their exit after Sheeran's Tuesday morning statement. "As musicians, playing to those crowds every night is the stuff of dreams but to play in venues that silence anyone advocating for a Free Palestine is simply not an option for us," the band wrote, adding: "We were there for Macklemore's performance and speech. We fully supported his message, so did most of the audience in Met Life Stadium which terrifies the lobbies." They also urged followers to research Kraft's work against the BDS movement.

FINNEAS pulled out Tuesday afternoon. "Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed," he wrote on Instagram. "I stand with Palestine and its people." Danish band Lukas Graham left the same afternoon, writing that "Money doesn't give you the right to own the conversation. Nobody's bank balance should decide who gets to speak or which suffering we're allowed to acknowledge," and closing the post with three watermelon emojis, a widely used stand-in for the Palestinian flag.

Irish singer Aaron Rowe also withdrew Tuesday afternoon, writing that "as Irish people we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation" and that he "cannot stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up against Israeli genocide." That leaves Sheeran without his backing band and three support acts, with the tour's remaining dates still on the calendar.
